en: The Hymn of Praise to Vāgīśvaravarṇa:
whose body is worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods, humans, and asuras;
who is the abode of all [perfections] such as knowledge; and who possesses the king of virtues.
I perpetually bow to the Lord of Speech, the preceptor of the gods, who is the sovereign of knowledge, composed of virtues, and possessed of the increase of excellence. || 1 ||
The sages praise him who is the knower of all mantras and the composition of the Vedas and other scriptures, whose words are perfectly sung through hymns, narratives, and the like,
and who understands the human voice.
I perpetually bow down to Vāgīśvara, the preceptor of the gods. || 2 ||
To him whose body is preeminent in wisdom, whose intellect is inconceivable, the Lord of Speech whose fame is praised in heaven and on earth;
to that Jñāneśvara, the Lord of the three worlds, who is both the moving and the unmoving.
I perpetually bow to Vāgīśvara, the preceptor of the gods. || 3 ||
The mind, which is the object of knowledge complete with the craftsmanship of jewels and other arts, variegated and adorned with diverse qualities, and worthy of the respect of people—
this mass of Brahman, the source of the omniscient one, resides within the heart.
I perpetually bow to Vāgīśvara, the preceptor of the gods. || 4 ||
In the ritual of conduct, one should meditate upon the Lord of Passion, whose awakening is firm and steadfast, the sovereign of meditation who is to be delighted by various methods,
the Guru established in Vidyā, who completely fills the world.
I perpetually bow down to Vāgīśvara, the preceptor of the gods. || 5 ||
I bow to that lotus-like face which bestows all desires upon the world, and to the Lord of Speech (Brahmā), who incessantly holds a book, a pen, an arrow, and a bow in his four arms, respectively.
I perpetually bow down to Vāgīśvara, the preceptor of the gods. || 6 ||
